Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
- 25-year-old female presents with three days of persistent, severe, right-sided headache with visual symptoms.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Sudden-onset "blinding" headache for three days, worst over right eye, persistent and severe (8/10, reduces to 5/10 after Ibuprofen but never resolves).
- Associated symptoms: Photophobia, intermittent "shooting lights" in vision, feeling generally unwell with some lack of energy.
- No nausea or vomiting. No focal neurological symptoms (no tingling, numbness, or weakness). No change in smell/taste. No sleep disturbance (able to fall and stay asleep, not woken by headache). Headache worse with standing up quickly or sudden head movements, but not clearly positional otherwise.
- No sinus, ENT, or respiratory symptoms. No recent fever (temperature not measured) and does not feel feverish.
- Past history: No significant past medical history. Remote, unexplained childhood pain episode.
- Medications: Combined oral contraceptive pill (specific name not documented, started one year ago, no side effects); Ibuprofen as needed (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: None known.
- Family history: Mother has severe migraines.
- Social history: Lives alone, works from home, had to take time off work due to headache. Non-smoker, consumes alcohol (approx. once weekly, three units). No recreational drug use.
- Recent well-woman checks: BP checked one year ago (normal). Recent eye check (no change in vision).

Examination:
- No physical examination performed during this consultation.

Impression:
- Likely migraine-type headache with visual disturbance; consideration of other causes of new, severe headache (e.g., secondary headache) requires in-person evaluation.

Plan:
- Book in-person consultation for neurological examination and fundoscopy.
- Check blood pressure at review (especially in context of combined oral contraceptive use).
- Prescribe stronger analgesic (specific medication not named) and recommend concurrent Paracetamol (dose/route/frequency not documented); advise taking with food.
- Advise ongoing use of the current contraceptive pill, but if diagnosis is migraine with aura, discuss switching to alternative contraception in future.
- Safety-net: Instructions to seek urgent medical attention if headache worsens, changes, or becomes unbearable before the scheduled appointment.
- Advise booking appointment with the support team for assessment.

Quality checks:
●	Missing but clinically expected: Name of contraceptive pill; dose/route/frequency for analgesics; allergy and medication reconciliation (no over-the-counter meds or supplements documented); vital signs and neurological/ophthalmological exam; full family history; documentation of temperature (not measured).
●	Internal conflicts: None noted.
●	Transcript quality: Clear, comprehensive history; no notable gaps in audio.
